column.text: Bitcoin is currently trapped in a fragile bullish bias, weighed down by extreme long skew and institutional ETF outflows of fifty-seven point six million dollars this morning while the ten-year yield spikes to thirty years highs. Retail sentiment remains aggressively long with leverage-to-short ratios at two point twenty-two for Bitcoin, yet smart money distribution via whale wallets creates a dangerous divergence where retail fuels the bid while institutions exit strength on technical momentum charts showing an RSI near sixty-nine point seven without follow-through volume. The tape is distinctly down-trending in this risk-off regime, meaning most continuation longs lack real proof of rising open interest and price action to survive immediate liquidations if key resistance fails again today. Dollar liquidity is contracting rapidly as retail money market assets hit record three trillion dollars while the government sells thirty-year treasuries at yields exceeding five percent, pushing all demand for crypto into a macro headwind that demands higher conviction on every entry. Short sellers now carry significant tailwinds through long-liquidation dominance and failed reclaim attempts of moving averages, whereas counter-trend longs are only viable as high-conviction reversals at clear exhaustion levels with specific catalysts rather than reflexive dip buys. The market is pushing into a liquidity vacuum where demand must prove itself on the tape before any breakout can sustain momentum against rising funding rates and negative macro headlines from Japan to Korea.
